[00:00] Evan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we've got about 45 minutes, quick agenda — renewal timeline, capacity needs, adding eu-west-1 region, security docs, and then next steps. sound good?

[00:52] Maya: and are you using prefix cache? i recall you had some heavy prompt reuse.

[01:10] Evan: okay, that informs sizing. so options: 1) add a Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 and keep us-west-2, 2) add regional routing to fall back to us-west-2, or 3) add smaller eu pool + cross-region fallback. tradeoffs are cost vs tail latency.
[01:27] Jordan: option 3 seems appealing — small eu pool for most traffic, fallback for heavy tails. what's the SLA implication?
[01:33] Luis: SLAs are per pool; adding a dedicated eu pool gives predictable throughput and you can set canary/fallback policies. if eu pool saturates, requests route to us-west-2 automatically if you enable cross-region fallback.
[01:46] Priya: on pricing, curious about committed term discounts — 1yr vs 3yr. we might be open to 3yr if unit cost savings are notable and we can get dedicated capacity guarantees.

[02:21] Priya: yep, next week works. we need results to share with execs.
[02:25] Evan: noted. i'll loop Maya to schedule.

[02:35] Evan: we can be flexible; typically monthly or annual invoicing; for committed discounts it's often annual or quarterly invoicing but we can discuss. i'll include billing options in the quote.
[02:45] Jordan: security — SOC 2 status, KMS integration, and whether logs are accessible for our auditors. we need to know data residency too.
[02:56] Luis: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report is available, we also support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured with audit logs and retention policies. i'll attach the SOC2 summary and a network diagram after this call.
[03:13] Carlos: for eu data residency, if we spin up eu-west-1 dedicated, does data stay in-region? any cross-region replication?
[03:21] Maya: yes, region-bound KV and model state stays within region by default. cross-region fallback will send inference requests to us-west-2 only if enabled as a policy; no automatic replication of customer data between regions unless you opt in.
[03:36] Priya: good. two more on compliance — can we integrate with our HSM/KMS and get encryption at rest for embeddings?
[03:44] Luis: customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated we have KMS integrations; i'll confirm the HSM compatibility matrix in the doc we send.

[04:26] Evan: yes — we can structure committed baseline with burst credits and add-on purchases. for longer terms we usually allow limited seasonal rebalancing; i'll work this into proposed contract language.
[04:36] Jordan: on performance, our key metric is 99th percentile < 300ms for short prompts. can you hit that in eu?
[04:44] Maya: we'll run tests; with a local eu pool + KV cache tuning and quantization profiles tuned for gen-6 models, hitting ~200-300ms 99th is feasible for short prompts. for long sequences or complex contexts tail can grow — the benchmark will surface that.

[05:07] Evan: yes, we can propose model_variant B (quantized) with ~30% lower per-token cost; Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles per workload.
[05:15] Priya: ok that's interesting. can that be part of the POC/benchmark?
[05:18] Maya: absolutely, we'll include a cost vs quality comparison in the benchmark run.
[05:22] Jordan: any blockers from your side?
[05:25] Priya: procurement will need clear SOW and billing terms before legal signs off; Sofia will manage that piece.
[05:31] Sofia: yes, i'll need the SOC2 and the contract with billing options and termination flexibility, plus a statement of work for the eu pool.
[05:40] Evan: will do. i'll also include a migration/onboarding checklist so your SREs know what to expect.
[05:48] Jordan: sounds good. can we recap next steps?
[05:52] Evan: yep. recap: Evan to send revised pricing and billing options by 7/9; Luis to share SOC2 summary, network diagram, and HSM compatibility by 7/8; Priya to send detailed volume and peak QPS by 7/10; Maya to schedule benchmark in eu-west-1 for week of 7/13 and run cost/quality comparisons.

[06:18] Evan: understood. any other questions?

[06:25] Luis: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route latency and token-level cost breakdowns and traces; we can give you a short walkthrough during onboarding.
[06:34] Jordan: great, thanks team.
